_comment: EIP-712 array-of-struct hashing shapes that are KNOWN-UNCOVERED by this fix: the device still mis-hashes them. These are PRE-EXISTING defects present on develop too (NOT regressions introduced by this PR), and they only affect NON-canonical nested arrays of custom structs (no mainstream payload -- Safe, Permit2, Seaport single-level and bulk OrderComponents[2][2], ERC-2612, ENS, CoW -- is affected). Each oracle messageHash below is the EIP-712 hashStruct(message) digest on which @metamask/eth-sig-util V4 and ethers v6 agree (oracle is unambiguous); the device produces a different value. These entries exist to (a) pin the oracle-clean expected hash so the limitation is precisely documented and machine-checked, and (b) keep them out of the device-signing auto-discovery (their filenames are intentionally NOT '*-data.json'). See test_eip712_known_uncovered.py and the PR's KNOWN LIMITATIONS section.

known_uncovered_gapA_structfirst_nested_.shape: Elem[2][2] where Elem's first field is a custom struct (Child)
known_uncovered_gapA_structfirst_nested_.note: Nested array (depth>=2, fixed or dynamic) whose element struct's FIRST field is itself a custom struct. Single-level Elem[]/Elem[2] (Class R) is fixed and matches; scalar-first nested arrays (Bug B, e.g. Seaport bulk) are fixed and match. This is the unhandled intersection of the Bug-B nested-array splice and the Class-R struct-first element-context selection at INNER array levels.

known_uncovered_gapB_empty_inner_struct_.shape: Leaf[][] with an empty inner array, message x=[[]]
known_uncovered_gapB_empty_inner_struct_.note: An empty CUSTOM-struct array occupying an INNER dimension of a multi-dimensional struct array. The scalar analogue uint256[][]=[[]] is correct on both develop and fixed, so the defect is specific to empty custom-struct arrays nested as an inner dimension. The Class-C empty-array repair handles only an empty array at FIELD position, not an empty array level whose enclosing context is itself an array accumulator.
